questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set 
$\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot 2+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 1+4\cdot (-4)+3\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -20 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{20\cdot 4+(-20)\cdot 5+0\cdot 0}{{4}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{1}=-\frac{20}{41}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{20\cdot 5+(-20)\cdot (-4)+0\cdot 0}{{5}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{0}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{180}{41}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =-\frac{20}{41}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+\frac{180}{41}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{20}{41}(-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+9[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}20 \\ -20 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** The projection is the vector $x$ itself. This means that $x$ can be written as a linear combination of $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$ In other words, $x$ lies in the subspace spanned by $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}.$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ 3 \\ -17\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\},$ $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\},$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{3}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4\cdot 1+6\cdot 1+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{1}=-\frac{24}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{4\cdot 3+6\cdot (-5)+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+(-5)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{35}{35}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{4\cdot 11+6\cdot 5+3\cdot 0+(-17)\cdot (-8)}{{11}^{2}+{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-8)^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{210}{210}[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}11 \\ 5 \\ 0 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ 0 \\ -17\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 2 \\ 31\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{v,w\}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set $\{v,w\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by 

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{(-9)\cdot 4+2\cdot (-4)+31\cdot 2}{{4}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{2}^{2}}v=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{(-9)\cdot 3+2\cdot 2+31\cdot (-2)}{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}w=-5[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-5[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-15 \\ -10 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-13 \\ -12 \\ 11\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 5 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\}$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{3\cdot (-1)+5\cdot 1+5\cdot (-1)}{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{1}=-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3\cdot (-3)+5\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 1}{(-3)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
